title: The effects of heat adaptation on physiology, perception and exercise performance in the heat: a meta-analysis
authors: Tyler CJ, Reeve T, Hodges GJ, Cheung SS
population: 96 articles on human heat adaptation regimens (PubMed to 16 Feb 2016); most common duration 7-14 days, most common method controlled work-rate
findings: Heat adaptation had a moderately beneficial effect on exercise capacity and performance in the heat irrespective of regimen; longer regimens were more effective than shorter ones.
Moderate-to-large beneficial effect on lowering core temperature before and during exercise, maintaining cardiovascular stability and improving heat-loss pathways.

Limited data: possibly reduced oxygen consumption, better glycogen sparing, higher power at lactate threshold, lower lactate, and better RPE and thermal sensation; trivial effect on extracellular Hsp.
Regimens lasting <14 days induce many beneficial adaptations and improve performance in the heat, but adaptation is greatest with regimens longer than 14 days.
Large methodological differences leave uncertainty about the magnitude and time course of adaptation.
limitations: Heterogeneous protocols; mostly young trained men in labs; outcomes mostly time trials or capacity tests, not marathon or ultra racing; Hedges' g values not in the abstract; the study unit is the article, not the participant.
implications: Default acclimation block: 7-14 days of daily heat exposure, extended beyond 14 days when time allows because adaptation is greatest with longer regimens.
Use acclimation as a conservative discount on the heat-pace penalty (shrink, do not remove); the abstract justifies no numeric discount.
No regimen type is shown to be superior in the abstract; do not encode a modality preference from this paper.

verification.notes: Crossref (Sports Med online 2016-04, print 2016-11) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched. Removed the researcher's 'prefer controlled-work-rate' implication, which the abstract does not support (it only reports that method as most common). The 5-day lower bound belongs to Daanen 2018.
